stemMd: In a closed terrarium, dead leaves are broken down by microorganisms. Which role of decomposers does this illustrate?

options.label: B
options.textMd: Returning nutrients in organic matter to forms that other organisms can use

options.label: C
options.textMd: Eliminating the need for an external energy input indefinitely

options.label: D
options.textMd: Turning every organism into a primary producer

explanationMd: Decomposers break down organic material and release nutrients that can re-enter biological cycles. They do not create matter or perfectly recycle energy. A terrarium can recycle many atoms internally while still depending on an energy input, usually light.

distractorRationale.a: Decomposition rearranges existing atoms rather than creating elements.
distractorRationale.c: Nutrient recycling does not remove energy losses as heat.
distractorRationale.d: Decomposition does not change all organisms’ trophic roles.
